behaviorDesc: The classic savanna antelope — grazes in small herds, pronks when startled, and can outrun anything you have except patience.
description: a small elegant antelope with lyre-shaped horns
diseaseVector: Cook through; gut quickly in heat.
huntText: The herd lifts its heads as one. Then the pronking starts — stiff-legged bounces — and they're gone in a dust line.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — lean red meat, a serious hunt's reward. The herd will be warier for days.

knowledgeLevels.1: Dorcas gazelle. Small antelope, elegant horns. Very fast.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (lean, excellent), hide (light leather), horns (tools), bones.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the savanna's deer — ambush at water in the dry season, or stalk with the wind in your face. They drink at dawn.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: dry-season waterholes are the trap — wait downwind before dawn. A bow at close range or a snare line on the game trail; never a chase you can't win.

name: Dorcas Gazelle
tell: the whole herd freezes, heads up, ears forward — the pronk comes next.
unknown: a small antelope bouncing stiff-legged through the heat shimmer

behaviorDesc: Troops raid, squabble, and post sentries. Clever, quick, and they learn — a troop you hunt today ambushes your snares tomorrow.
description: a grey-green monkey with a black face
diseaseVector: Primates share our diseases — cook thoroughly, avoid bites and blood contact.
huntText: The sentry barks once and the troop explodes into the trees — all but one, tangled in the low branches.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — stringy but real meat. The troop will remember your face; hunt far from here next time.

knowledgeLevels.1: Vervet monkey. Grey-green, black face, troops. Clever.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (tough, cook long), bones.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: trap or snare at fruiting trees; they raid crops and camps, so they come to you. Watch for the sentry — no sentry call means no monkey.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: they learn fast — rotate trap sites, never hunt the same troop twice in a row. Their alarm calls also warn you of leopards and snakes.

name: Vervet Monkey
tell: a sharp barking alarm — the troop's sentry has made you.
unknown: a grey-green monkey watching you from a branch, unimpressed

behaviorDesc: Bursts from the grass with a whirring cackle, flying low and fast. Coveys scatter — mark where each lands.
description: a plump brown partridge with a double spur
diseaseVector: Cook through.
huntText: The grass erupts — brown wings, cackling, low and fast. One peels off from the covey.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — small but fine game bird. Mark the covey's landing; they'll hold again.

knowledgeLevels.1: Francolin. Plump brown game bird. Bursts from grass.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (good), feathers.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: flush at dawn from thicket edges; snare at dust baths. Coveys hold territory — learn their ground.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: walk the thicket edge slowly at dawn; when one flushes, watch the rest land and work them one by one.

name: Double-spurred Francolin
tell: a harsh cackling from deep in the grass — the covey is about to flush.
unknown: a plump brown bird freezing in the grass, hoping you didn't see

behaviorDesc: Fearless beyond reason. It will stand down a leopard, eat a scorpion, and raid your camp for the honey — in that order.
description: a stocky black-and-grey mustelid with massive claws
diseaseVector: Aggressive biter — avoid the mouth; cook through.
huntText: It turns to face you — grey mantle, black belly, zero fear. This one decides if there's a fight.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — but what a fight. Thick loose skin, claws like garden tools. You earned every bite.

knowledgeLevels.1: Honey badger. Stocky, grey back, black belly. Fearless — do not corner it.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (tough), famously thick loose hide (armor-grade leather), claws.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: hunt only with a spear and respect — it twists inside its own skin to bite back. The hide is the real prize.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: they follow honeyguide birds to hives — find the bird, find the badger. Strike from behind the head; the skin slides and the teeth find fingers.

name: Honey Badger
tell: stands its ground, head low, making a rattling growl — it is not bluffing.
unknown: a stocky grey-and-black shape digging with total confidence

behaviorDesc: Strides the grassland in pairs, hammering the ground for snakes and tortoises. Huge, loud, and utterly unafraid of you.
description: a huge black-and-white ground bird with a massive bill
diseaseVector: Cook through.
huntText: It doesn't fly — it strides away, booming, too big to hurry. You can walk it down if you're patient.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — big bird, dark meat. It eats snakes for a living; the favor is returned.

knowledgeLevels.1: Ground hornbill. Huge, black-and-white, walks. Not afraid.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (dark, substantial), massive bill (tool material), feathers.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: stalk in the open — they can't fly far and they know it. Pairs hold big territories; learn the pair's route.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: they hunt cooperatively, flushing prey to each other — watch a pair work and you'll learn where the snakes den, too.

name: Abyssinian Ground Hornbill
tell: a deep booming call that carries a mile — the pair talking.
unknown: a huge black-and-white bird striding through the grass like it owns it

behaviorDesc: Suns on the rocks in a pile, scattering at a shadow. Quick, small, and everywhere there's stone.
description: a plump guinea-pig-like animal with rubbery padded feet
diseaseVector: Cook through.
huntText: The rock pile erupts — a dozen plump bodies scattering for the crevices. One hesitates.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — small but tender. The colony's sentry saw you coming; next time come quieter.

knowledgeLevels.1: Rock hyrax. Plump, rock-dwelling, quick.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (tender, small), hide (soft).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: snare at rock crevices at dawn; they sun in the same spots daily. The sentry's whistle is your warning.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: learn the colony's sunning rocks — set snares on the approach paths, not the rocks. Their middens mark the best spots.

name: Rock Hyrax
tell: a sharp whistle from the rocks — the sentry has spotted you.
unknown: plump shapes piled on a sun-warmed rock, scattering at your shadow

behaviorDesc: A ton of muscle with a bad attitude and no reverse gear. Buffalo don't bluff — if it lowers its head, the conversation is over.
description: a massive black buffalo with bossed horns
diseaseVector: Cook through; gut carefully.
huntText: It turns — massive head, horns like a battering ram. It is deciding whether you are a problem. You are.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — a mountain of meat. This was the most dangerous thing you've done this month. Butcher fast, guard the carcass, and expect company.

knowledgeLevels.1: African buffalo. Huge, black, horned. One of the most dangerous animals alive — never hunt alone.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (enormous quantity), thick hide (the best leather), horns (tools), fat, bones.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: a herd animal — hunt the straggler, never the herd. Spear from ambush with an escape tree picked in advance. Lions do it; you can too, carefully.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: old bulls separate from the herd — the target. Wound it and it WILL come for you; finish fast or climb. A buffalo kill feeds the village for a week — and the lions know it.

name: African Buffalo
tell: lowers its massive head and paws the dust — the last warning you'll get.
unknown: a black wall of muscle with horns, watching you back

behaviorDesc: The reason the savanna goes quiet at dusk. Lions hunt in prides, see in the dark, and consider you a rounding error.
description: a tawny lion, scarred and utterly confident
diseaseVector: Apex predator — cook through; never eat a sick-looking animal.
huntText: The grass parts and it's just THERE — tawny, scarred, looking at you the way you look at lunch.
killText: About {kcal} kcal. You killed a lion. Tell this story for the rest of your life — quietly, because the pride heard it too.

knowledgeLevels.1: Lion. Tawny, huge, pride hunter. The apex. Avoid.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (tough), hide (prestige), claws and teeth (tools, trade).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: hunt only in desperation or defense — a spear, a tree behind you, and friends. Lions hunt at night; your fire is your wall.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: a lone old male separated from the pride is the only sane target. Never hunt near a kill — the pride owns it. Your best defense is never needing one: fire, noise, numbers.

name: Lion
tell: the savanna goes quiet — birds stop, monkeys freeze. Something big is moving.
unknown: a tawny shape in the grass, too big, too calm

behaviorDesc: Stays in water. Nests in the shallows, guards its young, and bites the hand that tickles it.
description: a deep-bodied silver-grey fish
diseaseVector: Raw freshwater fish can carry parasites. Cook it.
huntText: A silver flash in the shallows — tilapia, circling its nest.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — clean white meat, the river's chicken. The males guard nests in the shallows; that's your window.

knowledgeLevels.1: Nile tilapia. Silver-grey, deep-bodied. Good eating.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (white, clean), bones (careful with the small ones).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: net or line in the shallows; they nest in circles on the bottom. A basket trap at the nest mouth is the patient hunter's play.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: breeding males are dark and aggressive — they guard, so they don't flee. Dawn in the shallows; the nest circles are visible from above.

name: Nile Tilapia
tell: circular cleared nests on the shallow bottom, a dark male hovering over each.
unknown: a flicker of silver over a cleared circle in the shallows

behaviorDesc: The night catfish — air-breathing, mud-walking, and strong enough to straighten a hook. Hunts by smell in the dark.
description: a dark eel-like catfish with long barbels
diseaseVector: Raw freshwater fish can carry parasites. Cook it. Watch the sharp pectoral spines when handling.
huntText: Something heavy moves in the dark water — a catfish, barbels sweeping, smelling its way to your bait.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — rich, fatty, no scales to fight. Mind the spines; they mean it.

knowledgeLevels.1: African catfish. Dark, eel-like, whiskered. Night hunter.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (rich, fatty, scaleless), spines (sharp — handle with care).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: night lines and basket traps; they walk between pools in the rains. Smelly bait wins.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: they breathe air — they survive in mud as pools dry. As the wetland shrinks, they concentrate. That's the harvest.

name: African Sharptooth Catfish
tell: a swirl in dark water and the smell of mud — it's hunting by scent.
unknown: a dark whiskered shape sliding through night water

behaviorDesc: The river's wolf — a huge silver predator that inhales smaller fish whole. Where the perch hunts, the water goes still.
description: a huge silver predatory fish
diseaseVector: Raw freshwater fish can carry parasites. Cook it.
huntText: The water goes still — then a silver torpedo rolls through the shallows, and the small fish scatter.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — a monster of a fish, steaks like a mammal. The river's top predator, on your fire.

knowledgeLevels.1: Nile perch. Huge, silver, predatory. The big one.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (thick white steaks), bones (large, useful).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: strong line or a big basket trap in deep pools. It hunts at dawn and dusk — be there.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: find the deep pool, fish the edges at first light. A perch this size needs a real line and patience; hand-fishing is a good way to lose a finger.

name: Nile Perch
tell: the small fish vanish all at once — something big is moving below.
unknown: a huge silver shadow turning slowly in the deep pool

behaviorDesc: Grazes in loose herds, bulls apart. Wary but not panicky — it watches you for a long time before deciding you're trouble.
description: a huge grey-blue antelope, the bull dark as slate
diseaseVector: Wild ruminants carry ticks; cook the meat through. Bulls in rut are dangerous — never corner one.
huntText: The herd lifts its heads as one. The blue bull stamps, decides, and they flow away like water — fast for their size.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — a mountain of lean meat, hide thick enough for real leather. The village eats for days.

knowledgeLevels.1: Nilgai — the 'blue bull'. Biggest antelope in Asia. The bulls are slate-grey, the cows tan.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (lean, lots of it), hide (thick — real leather), horns (tools, trade). Gut quickly; the size works against you in the heat.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: a single bull feeds the village for days. Bulls raid crops and know it — they're bold near fields, wary in the open.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: stalk at midday when they doze; the herd posts no sentries but every head lifts together. Take the shot from downwind — they wind you before they see you.

name: Nilgai
tell: freezes broadside, head high, ears swiveling — measuring you.
unknown: a slate-grey bulk at the meadow's edge, too big for a deer

behaviorDesc: Grazes in herds at dawn and dusk, melting into cover at midday. Spotted coat breaks up in dappled light — look for movement, not shape.
description: a spotted deer, white dots on russet, moving in a herd
diseaseVector: Deer carry ticks; check yourself after the butcher. Cook the meat through.
huntText: White spots scatter like thrown dice. The herd bounces away in great leaps — the white rump patches flashing the alarm.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — tender venison, a spotted hide worth trading. The herd will remember this meadow for a week.

knowledgeLevels.1: Chital — the spotted deer. Herds of them, dawn and dusk.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (tender), hide (spotted — trade value), antlers (tools, in season on the stags).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the tiger's favorite meal — where chital graze boldly, no tiger is near; where they've vanished, one is. Read the herd like a weather vane.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: hunt the edges at first light. The herd's alarm bark is your early warning too — learn it, and you'll hear tigers coming before you see them.

name: Chital
tell: the whole herd's heads come up at once; one barks — a sharp, dog-like yap.
unknown: russet shapes with white spots, flowing between the trees

behaviorDesc: Struts in the open, absurdly visible — then explodes into flight, screaming. The males display at dawn; the sound carries a mile.
description: a peacock in full impossible blue-green display
diseaseVector: Wild birds can carry mites; cook the meat through.
huntText: The tail goes up like a sail — a hundred eyes watching you. Then the scream, and it's airborne, heavy and loud.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — rich dark meat. The tail feathers are trade goods; the crest feathers mark a hunter.

knowledgeLevels.1: Indian peafowl. The national bird — impossible blue, louder than it looks.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (rich, dark), tail feathers (trade), eggs (in season, if you find the nest — the hen hides them well).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the dawn display is a clock — the males call at first light whether you sleep or not. Their alarm scream warns of leopard and tiger too.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: hunt at midday when they dust-bathe and doze. The males can't fly far with the full train — in display season they're almost catchable.

name: Indian Peafowl
tell: freezes mid-strut, neck up, listening — then the scream.
unknown: a flash of impossible blue-green, and a scream like a rusty gate

behaviorDesc: Trotts the trails alone, nose down, utterly unconcerned by you. It is hunting snakes — and it is very good at it.
description: a grizzled grey mongoose trotting the trail, nose down
diseaseVector: Mongoose can carry rabies — never handle one alive, and cook the meat hard.
huntText: It stands up on its hind legs to look at you — bold as brass — then drops and flows into the grass like water.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — small, musky, better stewed long. The pelt is coarse but warm.

knowledgeLevels.1: Indian gray mongoose. The snake-killer — it hunts cobras for a living.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (stew it long), pelt (coarse). Watch one work a thicket and you'll learn where the snakes den.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: a mongoose working confidently means snakes are about — follow at a distance and note the dens. They eat the eggs of ground-nesting birds too.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: they're curious and trap-shy in equal measure. Snare the runs, not the animal — and never corner one; the teeth are needles and the temper is real.

name: Indian Gray Mongoose
tell: rears up on its hind legs, nose working — deciding if you're worth the trouble.
unknown: a grizzled grey shape flowing through the grass, quick as a snake

behaviorDesc: Circles the camp at night, bold and clever. Takes the weak, the young, the unwatched — and your drying meat if you let it.
description: a lean wild dog, tawny and sharp-faced, circling at dusk
diseaseVector: Wild dogs carry rabies and mange — never handle one alive. Cook the meat hard.
huntText: It doesn't run far — just out of reach, turning to watch you with yellow eyes. It knows exactly how fast you are.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — lean dog-meat, hunger food. The pelt is decent; the skull is a warning to the pack.

knowledgeLevels.1: Golden jackal. The camp follower — bold, clever, always watching.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (lean, hunger food), pelt (decent), bones (tools). Hang your drying meat high — they can jump.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the jackal's dusk chorus tells you the wild is settling. A silent jackal is a frightened jackal — something bigger is moving.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: trap the trails, not the animal — they're trap-shy after one scare. And guard the drying racks: a jackal that's tasted your meat will bring the pack.

name: Golden Jackal
tell: stops just out of range and looks back — calculating.
unknown: a tawny dog-shape melting between shadows at dusk

behaviorDesc: Troops raid the camp in daylight, fast and organized — one distracts, the rest steal. They know what food looks like.
description: a troop of pink-faced monkeys raiding with military precision
diseaseVector: Monkeys can carry diseases transmissible to people — cook the meat hard, and never let them bite.
huntText: The lookout barks — and the troop explodes in every direction, chattering insults over its shoulder.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — the troop will remember this and avoid the spot for a week. Stringy but filling.

knowledgeLevels.1: Rhesus macaque. Clever, organized, and already stealing your lunch.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (stringy, stew it). The real harvest is knowledge: watch what the troop eats — monkeys test fruit you'd be afraid to touch.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: a troop feeding calmly means no predator is near; a troop screaming means leopard or tiger. Their alarm calls are a free early-warning system.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: never feed them — a fed troop becomes a raiding troop. Hunt the old males first; the troop scatters further without its lookout.

name: Rhesus Macaque
tell: the lookout goes still, staring past you — the troop is already moving.
unknown: chattering shapes flowing through the branches, quick hands everywhere

behaviorDesc: Waddles the night trails, rattling its quills at everything. It cannot shoot them — but backing into them is bad enough.
description: a waddling barrel of quills rattling in the dark
diseaseVector: Cook the meat through. The quills are the real danger — they work inward.
huntText: The quills go up with a rattle like dry reeds. It turns its armored back on you and waddles — daring you.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — rich meat, and a harvest of quills: awls, needles, fishhooks, trade goods.

knowledgeLevels.1: Indian crested porcupine. A barrel of quills that rattles when annoyed.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (rich), quills (awls, needles, fishhooks — the best small tools in the land), gut (eat fresh).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the quills are worth more than the meat — a porcupine is a toolbox walking. They dig for roots and bulbs; follow the diggings.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: hunt with a spear from the FRONT — the back is all quills. Dogs learn this once, painfully. Collect the shed quills along the trails for free.

name: Indian Crested Porcupine
tell: quills rise with a dry rattle; it turns its back — the armored end.
unknown: a rattling waddle in the dark, quills catching the moon

behaviorDesc: Darts along branches, chattering, tail flicking. Eats fruit and nuts — and will show you which trees are bearing.
description: a tiny striped squirrel flicking its tail on a branch
diseaseVector: Small rodents carry ticks; cook it if you bother.
huntText: Up the trunk it goes, chattering scolding all the way — stopping just out of reach to tell you exactly what it thinks.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — a mouthful. Hardly worth the chase unless you're truly hungry.

knowledgeLevels.1: Indian palm squirrel. The three-striped scold of the groves.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: barely a mouthful of meat. The value is the scolding: it alarms at snakes, owls, and cats.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: follow the scolding — a squirrel mobbing something low in a bush has found a snake. The legend says the stripes are Rama's fingerprints; the forest says they're camouflage.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: not worth hunting — worth listening to. Learn its alarm calls and the grove tells you everything.

name: Indian Palm Squirrel
tell: freezes mid-branch, tail flicking, then the chattering starts.
unknown: a striped flicker scolding from the branches

behaviorDesc: Feeds at dawn and dusk, freezing flat between hops. Fast but predictable — after the first juke it runs straight.
description: a large hare with a black-nape patch, freezing between hops
diseaseVector: Hares carry ticks and tularemia risk — wear gloves gutting, cook through.
huntText: It freezes. You hold your breath. Then — ears flat — it bolts, juking once before the straight run.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — lean meat, a solid meal. All protein, no fat: eat it with something greasy.

knowledgeLevels.1: Black-naped hare. Big ears, black patch on the neck, fast.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (lean), hide (thin), bones (tools). Gut quickly in the heat.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: protein, but lean — hare alone is rabbit-starvation food. The jackals hunt them at dusk; hunt where the jackals hunt.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: snare the runs at dawn. They follow the same paths nightly — find the trail, set the snare, walk away.

name: Black-naped Hare
tell: locks mid-hop, ears swiveling toward you.
unknown: a brown blur with tall ears, freezing between hops

behaviorDesc: You will not see it coming. It hunts from cover at dawn and dusk, and it learns: the same tiger works the same ground for years.
description: stripes flowing through the grass — a tiger, and it has seen you first
diseaseVector: Apex meat — cook thoroughly; big cats carry parasites. And the claws: clean any scratch like your life depends on it.
huntText: The grass parts without a sound. Two amber eyes, and then the whole striped avalanche of it.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — a mountain of meat, a pelt worth a kingdom, and a story no one will believe. The forest goes quiet for days after.

knowledgeLevels.1: Bengal tiger. The striped king. It has seen you first — it always has.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (rich, cook hard), hide (the prize pelt), claws and teeth (trade), fat (burns long). A kill this size must be guarded — everything comes to steal it.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the tiger's ground is the richest ground — where it hunts, the deer are fat. Read its scratch-marks on trees like a map: fresh marks, fresh tiger.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: it hunts what isn't watching. Never turn your back — face it and it hesitates. The Sundarbans trick is real: eyes on the back of your head, or just never look away. And never hunt a tiger alone.

name: Bengal Tiger
tell: the birds go silent all at once — and the grass stops moving the way wind moves it.
unknown: stripes flowing where no wind blows

behaviorDesc: Cruises the mid-water in schools, nosing the bottom. Spills at the surface at dawn — watch for the rings.
description: a big silver carp rolling in the water
diseaseVector: Raw freshwater fish can carry parasites. Cook it.
huntText: A silver roll at the surface — rings spreading. The school spooks at your shadow and the water goes still.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — firm white flesh, the classic curry fish. Watch the fine bones.

knowledgeLevels.1: Rohu. The big river carp — silver, deep-bodied, everywhere.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (firm, white), bones (fine — eat carefully), head (the richest part; the old hands fight over it).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: ~2000 kcal a good fish; the pond-and-river staple. Smokes and dries well for storage.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: fish the deep pools at dawn with dough balls. After the first monsoon spate, they run — be at the creek mouth.

name: Rohu
tell: rolls at the surface, showing a silver flank — feeding in the mud below.
unknown: silver rolls breaking the surface at dawn

behaviorDesc: Feeds at the surface, big mouth up — the rings it leaves are wider than rohu's. Bolder than the other carps.
description: a huge-headed carp gulping at the surface
diseaseVector: Raw freshwater fish can carry parasites. Cook it.
huntText: A great blunt head breaks the surface with a gulp. It doesn't spook easy — it owns this pool.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — the biggest of the river carps, meat by the slab. A feast fish.

knowledgeLevels.1: Catla. The surface-feeder — huge head, huge appetite.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (slabs of it), bones (fewer and bigger than rohu's — easier eating), head (soup fish).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the fastest-growing fish in the pond; a stocked tank is a bank account. Dries into slabs that keep months.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: surface bait at dusk — it feeds looking up. In the monsoon it moves into the flooded fields; follow the water.

name: Catla
tell: gulps at the surface, wide rings — feeding with its big mouth up.
unknown: a huge blunt head breaking the surface

behaviorDesc: Runs upriver in shimmering schools in the monsoon — the most famous fish in Bengal. Rich, bony, and worth every bone.
description: a silver shad flashing upstream in the monsoon run
diseaseVector: Raw freshwater fish can carry parasites. Cook it — steamed in mustard, traditionally.
huntText: Silver flashes in the current — a school pushing upstream against the monsoon flow, relentless.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — the queen of fish: rich, oily, famously bony. Eat slowly and with respect.

knowledgeLevels.1: Hilsa (ilish). The monsoon fish — all of Bengal waits for the run.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (rich and oily), bones (many, fine — the price of the flavor). Steam it; don't waste a drop of the oil.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the oil is the point — calories and flavor no other fish here matches. A monsoon run can fill the drying racks in days.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: be at the creek mouths when the first spate hits — the schools push upstream on the rising water. Net the run, not the fish.

name: Hilsa
tell: the water shimmers upstream in pulses — a school moving as one body.
unknown: silver shad flashing in the monsoon current
